subject: Follow-up: procurement & marketplace path (AWS/GCP/Azure) — next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Anna Torres <anna.torres@lumenai.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: procurement & marketplace path (AWS/GCP/Azure) — next steps

Hi Anna —

Great conversation this morning, thanks for making time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on procurement path: 

Recap from call:
- LumenAI is evaluating Redwood for inference (text+embeddings) for your analytics product.
- Primary procurement owners: you + Evan Lee (procurement@lumenai.com).
- Targeted go-live for pilot: mid-January.
- Expected initial spend: ~$30k/month, scaling after pilot.

Procurement/commercial questions we discussed:
1) Payment method: do you want to purchase via corporate card or issue a PO?
2) Marketplace: are you able/interested to buy via AWS/GCP/Azure Marketplace (listings available)? Using a marketplace path will simplify procurement and allow LumenAI to consolidate billing.
3) Contract path: if direct (PO), do you need a Redwood MSA + SOW? Any standard redlines we should expect from legal?
4) Timeline & approvals: what are the internal approval steps and estimated lead times for each?

Attachments I’m including: Redwood-Marketplace-Pricing-Guide.pdf (marketplace vs direct pricing notes) and Redwood-SOW-Template.docx (example SOW we use for pilots).

Proposed next steps:
- Can you confirm preferred commercial path (Marketplace vs PO/card)?
- If Marketplace: which provider (AWS/GCP/Azure) and who on your side owns the marketplace procurement?
- If PO: please share PO process owner and any required contract templates or redlines.
- If useful, I can loop in our Contracts lead (Jonas) to a short call to align on redlines.

Thanks — happy to move whichever route is easiest for you.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Redwood-Marketplace-Pricing-Guide.pdf (PDF, 120KB); Redwood-SOW-Template.docx (DOCX, 45KB)

From: Anna Torres <anna.torres@lumenai.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Lee <evan.lee@lumenai.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: procurement & marketplace path (AWS/GCP/Azure) — next steps

Thanks Camila — useful summary. A few clarifications from procurement side: 

- Preferred payment: we generally prefer to use Purchase Orders (PO) for new vendor commitments > $10k/month. We can do a corporate card for onboarding credits or one-off purchases but PO is likely.
- Marketplace: we do prefer Marketplace for ease of billing, but it depends on pricing parity and contract terms. We are on AWS primarily; GCP is secondary.
- Marketplace owner: Evan will own the marketplace intake; I own the PO process and final approvals.
- Contract: Legal will want to review Redwood MSA. We rarely accept vendor contracts as-is; there will likely be a handful of standard redlines (indemnity limits, data processing clauses). Expect a 2–3 week review once legal has the doc.

Questions for you:
1) If we go through AWS Marketplace, will Redwood provide the same pricing/discount profile as direct PO? Any differences we should budget for?
2) Are there invoice/term differences (Net30 vs Net45) between marketplace and PO purchases?
3) Any technical prerequisites for using Marketplace SKUs (account mapping, linked accounts)?

Can you send a quick note on those items and we can schedule a short 30-min sync with Evan and legal next week.

Thanks,
Anna Torres
Procurement Manager, LumenAI
anna.torres@lumenai.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up: procurement & marketplace path (AWS/GCP/Azure) — next steps

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear breakdown. Answers inline below: 

1) Pricing parity: In most cases Redwood maintains list-price parity across channels; however, contracted discounts and committed reserved capacity (Dedicated) can differ. For a pilot of your size (~$30k/mo), the economics are generally similar on AWS Marketplace vs direct PO. I attached a short pricing guide that highlights typical differences (see Redwood-Marketplace-Pricing-Guide.pdf).

2) Invoice/terms: Marketplace billing is handled via AWS invoicing and typically follows your AWS payment terms. For direct PO purchases with Redwood, our standard is Net30 but we can negotiate Net45 for enterprise finance teams. If your company requires PO + Net45, we can accommodate that in a direct deal.

3) Technical prerequisites: For AWS Marketplace purchases we ask customers to provide the AWS account ID(s) that will be billed/linked so we can map SKUs. There is no additional infra work on your side beyond standard account linking (no data plane changes). For GCP/Azure, similar account mapping processes apply.

Next steps I recommend: 
- If you prefer Marketplace: Evan, could you confirm the AWS account ID and whether your AWS billing owner can approve an AWS Marketplace procurement?
- If you prefer PO: Anna, could you share your PO template and any non-negotiables so Jonas and I can start a draft MSA with your terms in mind?
- Either path: propose a 30-min call Wed or Thu next week to finalize the route and timing.

Jonas — tagging you for legal/contract questions; happy to loop you into a call if needed.

Best,
Camila

Attachments: Redwood-Marketplace-Pricing-Guide.pdf; Redwood-SOW-Template.docx

Hi all —

Quick note from Contracts: happy to engage. A couple items to speed review if you go PO route: 
- Please send any vendor addenda or required clauses up front (data residency, SOC2 references, insurance minimums).
- We typically accommodate limited indemnity and mutually agreed DPA language.
- If LumenAI requires a signed PO first, we can accept PO + signature on MSA after — we'll just need a final version of your PO terms.

If you go Marketplace, legal review is usually much lighter since billing is through AWS and Redwood's MSA can remain standard for data processing. Camila, if you can share a short one-page summary of redlines we see most often that would be helpful for Anna's legal.

Available for a 30-min call Wed 12/2 or Thu 12/3 between 10am-2pm PT.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
